BEHIND THE WONDER

A real sky.
A space to experiment.

The observatory uses 5,044 catalogue stars with J2000 coordinates, transformed for your date and location. This prototype includes precession and nutation, but omits stellar proper motion, aberration, and atmospheric refraction. It is an educational sky view, not a precision ephemeris.

The studio starts with a 1-solar-mass model. Add a companion to explore Newtonian gravity. Luminous tracers are an artistic material, not a plasma simulation. Painted trails are cleared when you move the time slider; body motion is replayed deterministically.

Fusion powers ordinary stars. Fusion experiments, chart imports, and full stellar evolution are planned; this version explores gravity and motion.

References: D3 Celestial · Astronomy Engine · NASA · Thomas Ricouard’s implementations
